issues.title: core -02: Rename subject_syntax value "uri" (misleading; accepts non-URI StringOrURI)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Queued for `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-assertion` -02. Deferred pre-`-01` publication; deliberately not edited on main until the -02 batch opens.

## Problem

The `instance_issuers` descriptor member `subject_syntax` defines the default value `"uri"`, described as "arbitrary StringOrURI" (§instance-issuers). The name is misleading: RFC 7519 StringOrURI permits any string without a colon, so the `"uri"` profile in fact accepts plain non-URI strings. An implementer reading the value name will assume URI-only validation that the spec does not require.

Renaming now, before a registry exists and implementations depend on the name, is cheap; renaming after IANA registration is the painful path.

## Options (from the review that queued this)

1. `uri` → `default` — acknowledges the value means "whatever StringOrURI permits"
2. `uri` → `string-or-uri` — names the actual syntax

## Affected text

- Core: `subject_syntax` definition and both defined values (§instance-issuers), plus every example descriptor using `"subject_syntax": "uri"`
- Companion impact: the agent profile's worked example (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-ai-agent-instance.md`) shows `"subject_syntax": "uri"` in its client-metadata example and needs the matching one-line update in its next rev

issues.title: core -02: State explicitly that assertion presentation is independent of token_endpoint_auth_method (public clients)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Queued for `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-assertion` -02. Deliberately not edited on main until the -02 batch opens.

## Problem

Core's token-endpoint processing step 1 says the AS authenticates the client "using its registered `token_endpoint_auth_method` per RFC 6749" and never mentions public clients or `none`. Core is *silent* on whether a public client (e.g., `authorization_code` + PKCE, no client credential) may present the `client_instance_assertion` parameter.

The agent profile now depends on the permissive reading: its "Local and Public-Client Agent Instances" section (added in #15) states "Presenting a Client Instance Assertion does not require confidential-client authentication; only CIA-CORE's instance-assertion authentication method does." That is an interpretation of core, not a statement core makes — an implementer of core alone could plausibly reject parameter presentation from unauthenticated clients, stranding the local-agent pattern (CLI/desktop agents are the most visible agent deployments).

## Fix

One sentence in core's presentation/processing text, roughly:

> Presentation of `client_instance_assertion` is independent of the client's registered `token_endpoint_auth_method`, including `none`; a public client MAY present a Client Instance Assertion.

Optionally note that the instance-assertion *authentication method* (`token_endpoint_auth_method: client_instance_assertion`) remains the only case where the assertion doubles as a client credential.

## Origin

Fresh review of the agent profile, 2026-07-04 (finding 4, resolved in the profile via PR #16's queue note; the actual fix lives here).

issues.title: core -02: Fix client_instance OAuth Entity Profiles registration (field names + Usage Location)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Queued for `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-assertion` -02. Deliberately not edited on main until the -02 batch opens.

## Problem

Core's IANA registration for the `client_instance` entity profile (§iana, ~line 2628) does not match the registry template actually defined by draft-mora-oauth-entity-profiles-01, in two ways:

1. **Field names.** Core uses "Profile Name / Profile Description / Profile Usage Location / Specification Document(s)". The registry template (§14.1.1 of entity-profiles) defines "Entity Profile Name / Entity Profile Description / Usage Location / Change Controller / Specification Document".
2. **Usage Location value.** Core registers "Actor Profile" only, but core's own surfacing rules place `client_instance` in the **top-level `sub_profile`** for self-acting (client_credentials-style) cases — which the registry classifies as "Subject Profile". The registration must read: `"Subject Profile", "Actor Profile"`.

## Precedent

The agent profile's `ai_agent` registration had the identical defect and was corrected in PR #16 (2026-07-04) after verifying the template against draft-mora-oauth-entity-profiles-01; core's fix should mirror that edit exactly.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body: Verified against draft-mora-oauth-entity-profiles-01: `client_instance` is NOT among the registry's seven initial entries (user, device, native_app, web_app, browser_app, service, ai_agent), so core's registration request is valid and this issue stands as written — fix the template field names and Usage Location only. Note the contrast: the agent profile's `ai_agent` request WAS a duplicate of an initial entry and was removed entirely (see PR #23).

issues.title: core -02: trust-model-as presumes a vetted registration channel (unauthenticated DCR / CIMD)
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Queued for `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-assertion` -02. Deliberately not edited on main until the -02 batch opens.

## Problem

§trust-model-as states the AS treats the registered `instance_issuers` list as **authoritative** — trust in an instance assertion derives solely from the client's registered metadata. The section considers AS-side issuer *additions* (they weaken the client's audit ability) but never the converse: whether the AS should apply policy before honoring a client-asserted list when the registration channel itself is unvetted.

That assumption holds for vetted registration but not for:

- **Unauthenticated dynamic registration (RFC 7591)** — the registrant is a party the AS has no relationship with
- **CIMD-identified clients (I-D.ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document)** — the entire metadata document, `instance_issuers` included, is authored and hosted by the client at a URL it controls. Core supports CIMD as a first-class registration model and handles its mechanics (dereference, caching, descriptor mutability) but is silent on this trust question.

The registrant gains nothing against *other* clients (per-client minting bounds the delegation), but the AS is still accepting a trust root from an unvetted source.

## Fix sketch

A security consideration (or a caveat in §trust-model-as): the authoritative treatment of registered `instance_issuers` presumes the metadata arrived through a channel the AS trusts; for unauthenticated registration or client-hosted metadata documents, the AS SHOULD validate listed issuers against AS policy (e.g., an allowlist of recognized issuers, or for RFC 7591, a signed software statement) before honoring them.

## Precedent

The agent profile generalized its equivalent subsection to "Attester Trust from Client-Asserted Metadata" covering both cases (PR #25, 2026-07-04); core's version should state the general principle for all clients, not just agents.

pulls.title: Narrower client-instance assertion profile with an optional attestation-evidence path
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Restructure as -01: dedicated client_instance_assertion parameter and layered composition with attestation-based client auth

Replaces the prior reuse of actor_token / actor_token_type on non-token-exchange grants with a dedicated client_instance_assertion request parameter. Token-exchange continues to use actor_token per RFC 8693.

Restructures the relationship with draft-ietf-oauth-attestation-based-client-auth from "two orthogonal specs" to a layered model: attestation-based deployments use that document as the wire mechanism with this profile applying surfacing rules on top via the new §Attestation-Based Instance Evidence path. Specifies cnf.jkt (JWK thumbprint per RFC 7638) as the fallback instance subject when no deployment-defined mapping is available.

Renames the token_endpoint_auth_method value to
client_instance_assertion. Adds client_instance_assertion_supported and client_instance_attestation_evidence_supported AS metadata.

Drops the generalized actor-token grant extension and the §Other Actor Token Types extension point; this profile no longer generalizes over arbitrary actor-token profiles. The grant extension can be revived as a companion spec if a second actor-token profile needs it.

See -01 Document History for the full change list.

pulls.title: Restructure to -01: dedicated CIA parameter, validation tightening, companion split
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Restructures the draft as -01 with a dedicated `client_instance_assertion` request parameter and splits the attestation-evidence composition into a separate companion document. Replaces the closed PR #1 (which was lost when the source branch was renamed from `client-instance-assertion-param` to `cia-restructure`).

Net diff vs main: 2057 insertions / 769 deletions across two files. Ten commits on top of `main`, each reviewable in isolation; commits are sequential (a later commit may rely on an earlier one being in place).

## What changed

### Wire surface

* Introduce the `client_instance_assertion` request parameter on `authorization_code`, `client_credentials`, `refresh_token`, and JWT bearer grants, with JOSE `typ` value `client-instance+jwt`. Token-exchange continues to present the assertion as `actor_token` with the registered URN `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:client-instance-jwt`. Drop the previous "actor token grant extension" framing and the generalization over arbitrary actor-token profiles.

### Scope

* Split the attestation-based instance evidence composition (with OAuth Attestation-Based Client Authentication) into a separate companion document, `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-attestation-evidence-00`. The companion owns the composition's processing path, security considerations, IANA "OAuth Client Instance Derived Subject URN Types" sub-registry (seeded with `jkt`), and `client_instance_attestation_evidence_supported` AS metadata. Core no longer normatively imports ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH.

### Access-token contract

* Require RFC 9068 for JWT access tokens and state the profile-level top-level claim set explicitly (`iss`, `aud`, `client_id`, `iat`, `exp`, `cnf`, `scope`, plus `sub`/`act`/`sub_profile` per classification).
* Add §rs-processing-introspection: the claim set in active introspection responses MUST equal the JWT access-token payload's claim set for the same grant.

### Validation procedure

* Define the optional `client_instance_assertion` token-endpoint authentication method (§instance-assertion-auth) with its validation procedure and `invalid_client` re-coding (covers both `invalid_grant`-class and `invalid_request`-class failures).
* Reorder §as-processing so PoP verification precedes the replay check, enabling the cnf-bound reusable-mode optimization in §security-replay.
* Specify octet-equality for `iss`/`sub`/`client_id`/`aud`/`spiffe_id` comparisons (no case folding, Unicode normalization, percent-decoding, or URI canonicalization), with the SPIFFE wildcard rule explicitly carved out.
* Specify `(iss, jti)` replay-cache scope: ASes MUST NOT widen the key with `client_id`; the cache is shared across clients listing the same instance issuer.
* §refresh now requires that a fresh Client Instance Assertion presented on refresh pass the replay check against its own `(iss, jti)`.

### SPIFFE

* Add §spiffe-compatibility for raw JWT-SVID presentation without re-minting, with sender-constraint established via an independent binding key per §spiffe-binding. Clarify that presence of `client_id` in the assertion selects re-minted mode unconditionally.

### Security

* New §security-multi-tenancy documenting the two-level class-and-instance model and recommending per-tenant `client_id` where tenants are independent trust boundaries.
* New paragraph in §security-trust-model noting the AS cannot verify issuer-side compliance with the per-client minting rule.
* Soften §trust-model-as restriction on AS-side issuer configuration from prescriptive to advisory.

### Signing and metadata

* Declare ES256 mandatory-to-implement; RS256 SHOULD-support.
* Define `instance_issuers` client metadata and the `client_instance_assertion_supported` AS metadata parameter.
* Establish the "OAuth Client Instance Subject Syntaxes" sub-registry (Specification Required), seeded with `uri` and `spiffe`, cross-referenced with the companion's "OAuth Client Instance Derived Subject URN Types" sub-registry to distinguish descriptor-side from token-side identifiers.

### Companion non-normative content

* Worked examples (self-acting with `cnf.jkt` URN fallback; token-exchange variant placing the URN in `act.sub`).
* Example Mapping Shapes appendix illustrating two real-world attestation ecosystems: OpenID4VCI wallet attestation (EU eIDAS 2.0 / EUDI Wallet) and ACME device attestation (`draft-ietf-acme-device-attest`, with Apple Managed Device Attestation as the most widely deployed realization).

### Editorial

* Retitle the core to "OAuth 2.0 Client Instance Assertion" (drop "Profile" and "using Actor Tokens"). Rewrite the abstract to lead with the artifact.
* Add a "Client Instance Evidence" defined term in §Conventions as the umbrella the companion's term inherits from.
* Worked examples in the core cover authorization-code, client-credentials, token-exchange, refresh (with and without a fresh CIA), the `client_instance_assertion` auth method, and SPIFFE JWT-SVID reuse.
* Trim operational/deployment content not in scope for an OAuth protocol spec: cross-instance-session-continuity recipes, specific TTL recommended defaults, "Defer adoption" bullet, agentic-framing in §Introduction, and §rs-processing's restatement of ACTOR-PROFILE.
* Invert and expand §Design Rationale.

## Commit sequence

1. `2dfdfd3` — Restructure as -01: dedicated `client_instance_assertion` parameter and layered composition with attestation-based client auth (already on the previous PR).
2. `80c15b4` — Trim operational content; align examples; tighten §rs-processing. WG-readiness pass, no normative change.
3. `822ade0` — Tighten validation procedure. Octet-equality; PoP-before-replay; auth-method `invalid_client` taxonomy; replay-check for fresh CIA on refresh; `(iss, jti)` cache scope.
4. `fcb4f6b` — Add SPIFFE/multi-tenancy clarifications, IANA registry, access-token claim set, introspection contract. New §security-multi-tenancy, §rs-processing-introspection, "OAuth Client Instance Subject Syntaxes" sub-registry; RFC 9068 alignment.
5. `e86c9d9` — Split attestation evidence into companion document.
6. `cd8f1fd` — Retitle to "OAuth 2.0 Client Instance Assertion"; final alignment. Title, abstract rewrite, Client Instance Evidence definition, plus late refinements (ES256 MTI, `actor_token` rejection on non-token-exchange grants, confidential-client carve-out, RFC8126 normative for the new sub-registry, three blocking review nits cleared).
7. `67aee93` — Add non-normative §Example Mapping Shapes appendix to companion (OpenID4VCI wallet attestation + ACME device attestation).
8. `817cf7b` — Simplify companion -00 Document History to a single "Initial publication" line.
9. `8bd9ecb` — Fix unresolved RFC8705 reference in companion (build error).
10. `ee38ef8` — Fix ACME-MDA appendix example to match DPoP combined-mode requirement (`cnf.jkt` instead of `cnf.x5t#S256`).

## Test plan

- [x] `kramdown-rfc` and `xml2rfc-html` render both documents without warnings or errors
- [x] All `{{anchor}}` cross-references resolve within each document
- [x] All RFC references in each document are declared in normative or informative refs
- [x] Cross-document references (`{{CIA-CORE}}`, `{{CIA-ATTEST-EVIDENCE}}`) use prose section names that survive rendering
- [x] IANA registries are independently reviewable (core's "OAuth Client Instance Subject Syntaxes" and companion's "OAuth Client Instance Derived Subject URN Types"; cross-linked)
- [x] CI build clean on every commit
- [ ] `idnits` clean for both documents (run pre-submission)

pulls.title: Tighten §access-token to profile-specific surfacing
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

§access-token previously restated RFC 9068's top-level claim set (`iss`, `aud`, `client_id`, `iat`, `exp`, `cnf`, `scope`) alongside the profile-specific surfacing rules. The restatement was redundant with RFC 9068 itself and made the section read like generic OAuth access-token plumbing inside a spec named for the Client Instance Assertion.

This PR removes the restatement and tightens §access-token to the three profile-specific surfacing rules:

* The access token MUST be sender-constrained per §sender-constrained (`cnf` bound to the instance's key).
* The validated instance identity surfaces in `act` (delegation) or top-level `sub` (self-acting); `sub_profile` signals the kind of subject.
* Any upstream actor chain MUST be preserved by nesting per ACTOR-PROFILE.

The generic JWT access-token contract is inherited from RFC 9068; the spec no longer restates it. Opaque (reference) tokens carry the same set of claims through introspection per §rs-processing-introspection.

## What's unchanged

* §access-token-classification (the grant → classification table)
* §access-token-delegation (how `act.iss/sub/cnf/sub_profile` derive from the validated assertion)
* §access-token-self-acting (how `sub` is placed when no other principal)
* §chain-merging (nested actor chains)

## Document History

The change folds into the existing -01 history bullet (the draft has not been published yet). The bullet is rewritten from "Access token contract" to "Access token surfacing" reflecting the narrower scope.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` passes for both documents
- [x] Cross-references to {{access-token}} from §token-endpoint preamble and §as-processing still resolve
- [ ] CI build clean (will run on push)

pulls.title: Drop CIA-ATTEST-EVIDENCE dependencies from the core
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Makes the core spec independent of `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-attestation-evidence`. After this PR, the core can be submitted to the IETF datatracker without any dependency on the companion; the companion can be published later (or never) without requiring changes to the core.

## What changed

* Removed CIA-ATTEST-EVIDENCE from informative references.
* Removed all `{{CIA-ATTEST-EVIDENCE}}` cross-references from §Introduction, §Conventions, §Relationships, §token-endpoint, §as-processing, §access-token-self-acting, §errors, §rs-processing, §Adoption, §Conformance, and §iana-subject-syntax.
* Dropped the **Client Instance Evidence** defined term in §Conventions (added solely to umbrella over the companion's evidence form). The core uses **Client Instance Assertion** throughout; no umbrella term is needed for a single-form spec.
* §Relationships ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH subsection rewritten to describe the two specs as orthogonal without forward-referencing a composition document. Deployments combining them present a Client Instance Assertion alongside a Client Attestation.
* §Adoption reduced from three options to two (Adapter pattern; Raw JWT-SVID compatibility).
* §Document History "Scope" bullet (which described the split into the companion) removed; -01 has not been published yet, so no change-tracking entry is needed.

## What's unchanged

The companion file (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-attestation-evidence.md`) is unchanged. Its normative reference to CIA-CORE still points at the core; that direction of dependency is intentional and unaffected.

## Net effect

* Core builds standalone (`make html` clean).
* Companion still builds (its CIA-CORE back-link is intact).
* Net diff: +18 / −89 lines on the core.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean for both documents
- [x] No remaining `{{CIA-ATTEST-EVIDENCE}}` references in the core
- [x] All local cross-references in the core resolve

pulls.title: Define "Client Instance Evidence" in the companion §Conventions
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

After PR #4 removed `CIA-ATTEST-EVIDENCE` dependencies from the core (including the **Client Instance Evidence** defined term), the companion's §Conventions still attributed that term to `CIA-CORE` — a stale attribution.

This PR defines **Client Instance Evidence** in the companion itself (where it's the primary user) and removes the false attribution.

## Changes

* §Conventions: drop **Client Instance Evidence** from the list of terms inherited from `CIA-CORE`.
* §Conventions: add a new definition of **Client Instance Evidence** as the umbrella concept, naming the two known forms (CIA-CORE's Client Instance Assertion, this document's attestation-based form).

## Net effect

The companion is now self-contained for the term it uses in its title, abstract, conformance section, and body. Other terms inherited from `CIA-CORE` (Client Instance Assertion, instance issuer, client instance, OAuth client) remain defined in the core.

## Test plan

- [x] No remaining false attributions to terms not defined in `CIA-CORE`

pulls.title: Pre-publication tightening: SPIFFE bundle validation, replay-cache note, subject-namespacing trim
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Three small tightenings before -01 submission. No new normative requirements, only clarifications of existing text. Net diff: +17 / −14.

## Changes

**1. §instance-issuers, `spiffe_bundle_endpoint` descriptor (item 7).** Previously only required `subject_syntax` to be `"spiffe"`. Now also explicitly requires the AS to validate assertions from this issuer under SPIFFE semantics per §spiffe-compatibility. Closes a deployment ambiguity where an issuer could publish via a SPIFFE bundle but emit non-SPIFFE-shaped subjects.

**2. §security-replay (item 6).** One added sentence noting that the shared `(iss, jti)` cache across clients listing the same issuer cannot enable cross-client replay (the key doesn't include `client_id`), but high-volume traffic under one client can pressure other clients' cache hits. ASes SHOULD apply per-issuer rate limits and bounded cache caps. No protocol change.

**3. §access-token-self-acting (item 5).** Trimmed the multi-issuer subject-collision text. The normative content (SHOULD apply namespacing, encoding is deployment choice, RS treats it as AS-issued) is preserved. Removed elaboration on ad-hoc separators (`#` is not appropriate when issuers are URIs) — operational guidance rather than spec text.

## Item 4 (RFC7800/9449/8705 references)

Verified — references in §claims are correct. No edit needed.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean for both documents
- [x] No new normative requirements; only clarifications and tightenings

pulls.title: Companion review fixes: activation policy, grant scope, attestation freshness
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Resolves four substantive findings from the pre-submission review of the companion, plus mechanical cleanup. Net diff: +52 / −14.

## Substantive

**1. Activation policy (§attestation-instance-evidence).** The path previously activated implicitly for any ATTEST-authenticated client on a supporting AS — silently changing the client's issued-token shape (`act` claims, URN subjects). New normative text: applying the path is AS policy established at registration time or out-of-band; an AS MUST NOT apply it to a client that hasn't agreed to receive CIA-CORE's instance representation.

**2. Applicable grants (§attestation-instance-evidence).** Now stated explicitly: the path covers the grants in CIA-CORE's classification table, and its activation substitutes for CIA-CORE's parameter-presence trigger (on token-exchange the path applies with no `actor_token` present — which the worked example already showed but the normative text never said).

**3. §security-attestation-freshness (new).** Instance-evidence freshness under this path = Client Attestation lifetime (hours/days in some ecosystems) + DPoP proof freshness. The DPoP proof proves recent key possession, not recent Attester endorsement. Deployments needing CIA-CORE-like currency (≤5-minute assertions) SHOULD require short-lived attestations and fresh evidence on refresh.

**4. RFC 8705 → informative.** Cited once, only to say TLS-cert binding falls outside this composition. Same reference-hygiene class as the core's RFC 6755 fix.

## Minor

* Mapping source 1: clarified no in-band mechanism exists for client-supplied mappings (registration-time/out-of-band only).
* CIA-CORE reference date refreshed to 2026-06 (matches the core's current date).
* §Conformance: per-request bullets separated from the implementation-level metadata-advertising requirement.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean for both documents
- [x] RFC 8705 citation still resolves (now from informative)

pulls.title: Add OAuth 2.0 AI Agent Instance Profile; retire attestation-evidence companion
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Two commits. Net effect on `main`: the document family becomes **core (published -01) + AI Agent Instance Profile (-00)**, with the parked attestation-evidence companion removed.

### Commit 1 — `f39fc53`: Add OAuth 2.0 AI Agent Instance Profile (-00)

New draft profiling CIA-CORE for AI agent deployments (agent platforms calling MCP resource servers). Successor direction to the parked companion: the agent claims are the product, the carrier is pluggable.

* **Agent instance claims**: `agent_instance_id` (REQUIRED, Attester-minted, stable, key-independent), `agent_platform`, `agent_model`, `agent_runtime` (EAT-aligned, AS-consumed, never surfaced verbatim).
* **Two evidence carriers** with identical claims and processing: Client Instance Assertion (CIA-CORE) and Client Attestation (ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH DPoP combined mode), plus a carrier-precedence rule.
* **Subject derivation**: instance subject = `agent_instance_id`; the AS MUST NOT derive subjects from key thumbprints. Key rotation preserves identity; refresh tokens keep CIA-CORE's key binding (rationale in appendix).
* **Attested delegation chains**: every actor entry corresponds to an instance that presented Attester evidence at its hop.
* **Trust tiers** (self-attestation / hardware-rooted / independent), six security subsections, four JWT claims registrations, `ai_agent` entity profile, Design Rationale appendix, and a full worked example (user-delegated agent → MCP server → sub-agent spawn → key rotation).

### Commit 2 — `fea677b`: Refinements + companion retirement

* CIA-CORE reference switched to the datatracker handle (core -01 is published; bibxml resolves).
* Surfaced `sub_profile` MUST include both `ai_agent` and `client_instance` — core-only resource servers keep classifying correctly. Examples updated.
* New §security-carrier-asymmetry: the CIA carrier gives the *client* control of the Attester set (`instance_issuers`); the attestation carrier gives it to the *AS*. Named explicitly with guidance.
* **Removed** `draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-attestation-evidence.md`: subsumed by the agent profile's attestation carrier, and its normative `cnf.jkt` subject fallback directly contradicts the agent profile's prohibition on key-derived subjects. Recoverable from git history.
* README regenerated for the two-document family.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean for both documents
- [x] CIA-CORE I-D handle resolves via bibxml
- [x] All `{{anchor}}` cross-references resolve
- [x] README lists exactly the two tracked drafts

pulls.title: Resolve expert-review findings on the agent profile
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Resolves all 11 findings from the expert review of `draft-mcguinness-oauth-ai-agent-instance`. Net diff: +218 / −50. Two of the three normative gaps were regressions — companion text that was absorbed conceptually but not textually during the rewrite (confirmed by diffing the retired companion at `d054406`).

## Normative gaps (findings 1–3)

* **`act.iss` on the attestation carrier** — restored: delegation cases MUST set `act.iss` to the Client Attestation issuer; self-acting cases retain the issuer with token state (per-instance revocation keyed on `(act.iss, act.sub)` depends on it).
* **Grant applicability + token-exchange trigger** — restored: the carrier covers CIA-CORE's classification grants; activation substitutes for the parameter-presence trigger; token-exchange applies with no `actor_token`. "Token-type matching" restored to the satisfied-steps list.
* **Discovery/metadata surface** — new §metadata: `ai_agent_instance_profile` (client; anchors the "registered for this profile" condition and constitutes the attestation-carrier agreement) and `ai_agent_instance_profile_supported` (AS). IANA registrations added; RFC 7591/8414 normative; worked example updated.

## Design weaknesses (findings 4–7)

* **`agent_model`** redefined as the Attester's characterization of the *primary configured model at evidence issuance* — explicitly not a per-request guarantee (routing/fallback models don't invalidate it). Token-lifetime and refresh-chain staleness added to §security-freshness; §refresh states stored-state refresh re-surfaces originating provenance; the example's model-gating bullet is annotated with its limits.
* **`agent_runtime`** gains a concrete member: `eat` (Entity Attestation Token, JWT compact or base64url CWT). RFC 9711 moved to normative. No more members-less registered claim.
* **`agent_instance_id`** uniqueness widened to per-Attester across all clients — removes the cross-client collision case and the tuple-evaluation burden.

## Minor (findings 8–11)

* Transaction Tokens positioning in §relationships (complementary; issuance-time vs intra-domain propagation).
* §chains: spawn permission is AS policy; chain merging preserves the spawner, so spawning cannot shed identity.
* §security-scope: `ai_agent` membership is Attester-determined; RSes MUST NOT derive security guarantees from the classification itself.
* Design Rationale: `sub`/`agent_instance_id` redundancy rationale; why generic `agent_*` names are registered early (coordination invited).

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean for both documents
- [x] All `{{anchor}}` cross-references resolve
- [x] Companion diff (`d054406`) re-checked — no other unported content

pulls.title: Address adoption-reality gaps: local agents, DCR trust, identity chaining
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Closes the three gaps from the adoption analysis ("could platforms like Codex or Claude adopt this?"). Net diff: +70 lines, no changes to existing normative text.

## Changes

**1. §local-agents (new section).** The most visible agent deployments are CLI/desktop agents on end-user machines running as public clients (auth-code + PKCE, no client credential) — previously unaddressed. Defines the platform-attested local session pattern: local instance generates its key, authenticates to the platform control plane, the control plane (as Agent Attester) mints evidence binding that key, and the instance presents it per the CIA carrier alongside its normal public-client flow. Clarifies that presenting an assertion does not require confidential-client authentication, and that local-session attestation vouches for session issuance and key binding, not host integrity (hardware-rooted host evidence composes via `agent_runtime`).

**2. §security-dcr (new security subsection).** In dynamic-registration flows (the MCP norm), `instance_issuers` and the profile flag arrive from an unvetted registrant. ASes SHOULD NOT honor them from unauthenticated registrations unless the Attester is validated against AS policy — allowlist of recognized platform Attesters or signed software statement (RFC 7591). Names AS-side allowlists as the expected pattern for ecosystems serving dynamically registered agent clients.

**3. §relationships: identity chaining.** `I-D.ietf-oauth-identity-chaining` (informative) positioned as complementary — it moves identity across domains (the cross-app-access pattern enterprise IdPs deploy for agent-to-MCP access) but defines no agent claims; an AS applying this profile at issuance carries agent identity into chained tokens.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean for both documents
- [x] All cross-references resolve
- [x] No `--` constructions introduced

pulls.title: Resolve fresh-review findings: downgrade protection, refresh scoping, registry alignment
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Resolves all findings from the post-merge fresh review of the agent profile. Two substantive normative fixes, one verified-against-source IANA correction, one new security subsection, plus editorial polish. Net: +81/-33 on one file.

## Substantive

**1. Evidence-omission downgrade closed (§metadata, §errors, §conformance).** `ai_agent_instance_profile: true` previously obligated the AS to validate and surface evidence but never required evidence to be *presented* — a compromised instance (or host malware in the §local-agents public-client case) could omit the assertion and obtain tokens indistinguishable from an ordinary client's. Registration now means the AS MUST require Agent Instance Evidence on every covered token request and MUST reject covered requests presenting none. `refresh_token` is excepted (refresh re-surfaces recorded originating state, so attribution is preserved), and registration or AS policy MAY exempt grant types not used by instances (e.g., control-plane `client_credentials`).

**2. Refresh continuity scoped to the Attester (§refresh, §errors).** The check compared `agent_instance_id` alone; since the subject is scoped to its minting Attester, same-id evidence from a *different* listed Attester would have passed the literal check. Fresh evidence on refresh MUST now be issued by the same Agent Attester and carry the same `agent_instance_id`.

**3. Entity-profile registration corrected (§iana-entity-profile).** Verified against draft-mora-oauth-entity-profiles-01: the registry template fields are "Entity Profile Name / Entity Profile Description / Usage Location / Specification Document", and Usage Location distinguishes Subject vs Actor. Registration updated to use the real field names and to list **"Subject Profile", "Actor Profile"** — the value appears in top-level `sub_profile` for self-acting tokens, not only in `act`. (Core's `client_instance` registration shares the defect; queued for core -02 along with an explicit public-client presentation statement.)

**4. New §security-local-keys.** Companion security text for §local-agents: binding keys on end-user hosts SHOULD use platform/hardware-backed keystores with short-lived evidence; the Attester's minting interface is part of the identity boundary (platform credentials suffice to mint instances attributed to the account), so minting SHOULD be session-bound, audited, and rate-limited.

## Editorial

- PKCE cited (RFC 7636, informative) at both uses
- `agent_runtime.eat`: JWT vs CWT form discrimination stated (period separators)
- §security-dcr: profile flag without `instance_issuers` implicates the AS-configured attestation carrier — token-shape obligation, no new trust root
- AS metadata "MUST publish" hedged to "in any authorization server metadata it publishes"
- Grant names consistently code-formatted

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` clean (kramdown-rfc + xml2rfc)
- [x] Zero unresolved anchors in rendered HTML
- [x] No em-dash or `--` constructions introduced

pulls.title: Record why the profile is not defined over ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH alone
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Captures the ATTEST-vs-CIA positioning analysis in the document itself, preempting the first question a WG reviewer will ask. Verified against ATTEST -09 before writing: no token representation, `sub` = `client_id` (instance identified only by its key), no RFC 8693/chain semantics, no introspection content, attestation JWTs designed for reuse across their validity period.

## Changes

- **New Design Rationale entry** "Why the profile is not defined over Attestation-Based Client Authentication alone", placed after "Why carrier-pluggable": ATTEST stops at authentication; every RS-visible property is CIA-CORE machinery on both carriers; dropping the dependency relocates ~half of CIA-CORE into this profile rather than removing it; the CIA carrier serves deployments the attestation carrier structurally cannot (keep existing client auth, client-controlled Attester set, SPIFFE, mTLS, short-lived evidence). Closes with the positioning line: ATTEST answers whether a genuine instance is authenticating; CIA-CORE defines what the resource server sees afterward.
- **One pointer sentence in §relationships** so the reader meets the rationale where the question forms.

+35 lines, appendix + one body sentence; no normative changes.

pulls.title: Record why no assurance-tier claim is standardized
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Final pre-submission design-rationale entry: preempts the predictable WG question "you named three assurance tiers, why didn't you register the claim?" The answer: tiers are AS-to-RS policy vocabulary rather than attested facts, the tier determination is an operational judgment made at trust-configuration time, and a registered claim would carry the apparent authority of the attested claims it summarizes. Deferring until deployments show convergent semantics; a later document can add one compatibly.

+15 lines, appendix only; no normative changes.

pulls.author: mcguinness

pulls.title: Fact-check pass: use ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH's defined term Client Attester
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Systematic fact-check of every externally-verifiable claim in the profile against the actual referenced texts (entity-profiles-01, attestation-based-client-auth-09, and CIA-CORE), prompted by the duplicate `ai_agent` registration caught in #23.

**Result: 21 claims verified correct, 1 discrepancy fixed.**

## The fix

ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH's defined role term is **"Client Attester"**; this document said "an ATTEST-CLIENT-AUTH Attester" in the three places it maps the Agent Attester onto that role (terminology definition, §carrier-attest, §conformance). Corrected, and "Client Attester" added to the imported terms in Conventions.

## Verified correct (no change needed)

Against **entity-profiles-01**: `sub_profile` is a space-delimited string list (their example: `"service ai_agent"`) matching our examples and MUST text; `sub_profile` within `act` nodes explicitly permitted; registry name; `client_instance` absent from initial contents (core's registration valid, issue #20 stands).

Against **attestation-based-client-auth-09**: attestation `sub` = `client_id`; `cnf` carries the Client Instance Key (grounding our carrier-precedence key-equality check); transport is HTTP headers (grounding our "presents no request parameter"); "DPoP Combined Mode" is their §7.3 term; combined-mode DPoP-key-MUST-match-`cnf` rule; their own error vocabulary exists for our §errors inheritance.

Against **CIA-CORE**: JWT bearer in the permitted grants; `act.cnf` in the representation rules; per-instance revocation keyed `(act.iss, act.sub)`/issuer+`sub` exactly as our §carrier-attest and worked example state; sub-space collision requirement; authorization-time consistency ("consent covers the client as a whole"); short assertion lifetimes (five minutes or less); refresh bound to same `cnf` key; "access-token classification" is core's actual term; assertion `sub_profile` is "one or more" names (our "SHOULD include" list semantics valid); `invalid_client` re-code condition matches our §errors parenthetical; `(iss, jti)` replay check; introspection surfacing.

## Test plan

- [x] `make html` and `make next` clean; regenerated -00 txt has zero long lines

pulls.title: Broaden Attester-trust consideration to client-asserted metadata (CIMD)
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

§security-dcr covered the unvetted-source trust question for RFC 7591 dynamic registration only. Clients identified by a Client ID Metadata Document (I-D.ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document) present the identical posture — the metadata document carrying `instance_issuers` and `ai_agent_instance_profile` is authored and hosted by the client at a URL it controls — and CIMD is where the MCP ecosystem is heading, so the profile's audience meets this case first.

## Changes

- Retitled the subsection to **"Attester Trust from Client-Asserted Metadata"** (anchor `#security-dcr` unchanged); the reasoning now covers both unauthenticated RFC 7591 registration and CIMD-identified clients
- Remedies split made explicit: software statements are a 7591 construct with no CIMD equivalent; AS-side Attester allowlists apply unchanged to both; for CIMD the AS MAY additionally condition on the provenance of the client identifier URL
- CIMD added as an informative reference

Core-side: core's §trust-model-as treats registered `instance_issuers` as authoritative, presuming a vetted registration channel — the general fix is queued as a core -02 issue.

- [x] No em-dash or `--` constructions
